indication: ** 47-year-old male presenting with lower back pain, right greater than left. Clinical query regarding possible urinary stones or vertebral anomalies. No reported fever or leukocytosis.
technique: ** Computed tomography was performed through the abdomen and pelvis (AP) without intravenous contrast. Axial images were obtained and reconstructed in sagittal and coronal planes.
findings:
**
The visualized upper abdominal organs are unremarkable. The liver demonstrates normal size and attenuation without focal lesions. The gallbladder is present without evidence of cholelithiasis or wall thickening. The spleen and pancreas are within normal limits for age. Both adrenal glands appear normal in morphology.
Regarding the renal system, both kidneys demonstrate normal size and symmetric enhancement patterns. There is no evidence of hydronephrosis or perinephric stranding. No radiopaque calculi are identified within the renal collecting systems or along the course of the ureters bilaterally. The urinary bladder is partially filled with smooth walls.
The gastrointestinal tract shows no evidence of bowel wall thickening or obstructive patterns. A small amount of diverticulosis is noted in the sigmoid colon, which is a common finding and appears non-inflammatory.
Evaluation of the musculoskeletal system reveals an acute, unstable fracture of the L2 vertebral body. There is significant loss of anterior and middle column height with retropulsion of a bony fragment into the spinal canal, resulting in narrowing of the central canal at this level. The remaining lumbar vertebrae maintain normal alignment and height. No other vertebral anomalies are identified. There is mild degenerative disc disease at L4-L5 characterized by slight narrowing of the intervertebral disc space and small marginal osteophytes. The visualized pelvic girdle and sacroiliac joints are intact.
The visualized portions of the great vessels, including the abdominal aorta, are of normal caliber without aneurysm. No free intraperitoneal air or fluid collections are seen.
conclusion:
**
Unstable fracture of the L2 vertebral body with associated spinal canal stenosis due to posterior fragment retropulsion. No evidence of associated retroperitoneal hemorrhage.
